name: Gibea
overview: Gibea is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Sheva. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional personal details or narrative provided beyond his lineage. As such, Gibea's profile remains concise, focusing primarily on his genealogical placement within Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Gibea means 'mound' or 'hill.' It is a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:49. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, and it stands as a straightforward personal name without additional titles or honorifics.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Gibea as the son of Sheva, establishing his immediate paternal relationship. Beyond this, no further family connections or relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Gibea's significance lies in his genealogical position within the tribe of Judah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 2:49. While the biblical record does not elaborate on his personal deeds or role, his inclusion in the genealogies underscores the importance of tracing the lineage of God's chosen people. This genealogical mention contributes to the broader biblical emphasis on heritage and covenantal promises through the tribe of Judah.
